source_audit: This formalizes the continuous dyadic-level extraction step in the Bourgain–Yehudayoff Monotone expansion flattening strategy (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1108.2555, proof of Lemma4.1, equations4.3–4.5). The extraction is proved directly for Haar integrals, with explicit constants and a support-volume-free low-tail estimate, and applied to the actual R1791 symmetric autocorrelation densities. No novelty claim is made for these analytic support lemmas. The reference is motivation, not an axiom. No exact finite-group energy or metric discretization is silently substituted for continuous energy. Normalizing mixed energy, self-energy conversion, metric BSG and SL2 product growth/escape remain open formalization obligations.

proof_scope: In progress. R1792 proves that a bounded nonnegative subprobability density whose self-convolution has squared L2 mass at least tau>0 contains a pair of dyadic level sets with quantitatively large weighted Haar multiplicative energy. The low tail costs at most8a in squared energy, with factor2 on the high part, without a finite-volume support hypothesis. Choosing a=tau/16 yields at most1+log2(max(1,16C/tau)) levels and a fourth-power loss in their number. The theorem is instantiated for the actual symmetric smoothed-autocorrelation iterate rho_k when integral rho_(k+1)^2>=tau; measurability, inverse symmetry and weighted level masses are included. Relative-energy normalization, self-energy conversion, metric BSG, SL2 product growth/escape, strict flattening and unconditional paid padding remain unproved.
